name: Kazakh
variety: Standard Kazakh of Kazakhstan, Cyrillic script; acoustic values from one female speaker from the Zhambyl region (McCollum & Chen 2021)
sources: McCollum, Adam G. & Chen, Si (2021). Kazakh. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 51(2), 276-298.
Vajda, Edward (1994). Kazakh phonology. In Edward H. Kaplan & Donald W. Whisenhunt (eds.), Opuscula Altaica: Essays Presented in Honor of Henry Schwarz. Western Washington University.
Kirchner, Mark (1998). Kazakh and Karakalpak. In Lars Johanson & Éva Á. Csató (eds.), The Turkic Languages. Routledge.
Muhamedowa, Raihan (2015). Kazakh: A Comprehensive Grammar. Routledge.

vowel_formants.speaker: adult female (one speaker, initial-syllable vowels of words in isolation, n = 272)

contrasts: front versus back vowel sets /e ɵ ɪ ʏ (æ)/ and /ɑ o ə ʊ/
two vowel classes: the short, reducible high vowels /ə ɪ ʊ ʏ/ (ы і ұ ү) and the full vowels /ɑ æ e o ɵ/, the latter about twice as long
velar /k ɡ/ versus uvular /q ʁ/, predictable from vowel backness in native words but free in loans
the vowel-glide units /ij/ (и) and /uw/ (у) behave as marginal phonemes
allophony: /e/ is diphthongal [i̯e], most clearly word-initially; /o/ and /ɵ/ also begin with a short rounded on-glide
voiceless plosives are aspirated, less so in connected speech; word-initial voiced plosives are prevoiced
velar obstruents occur with front vowels, uvular ones with back vowels; /q/ is often a fricative [χ] in connected speech and /χ/ may be velar [x]
plosives are spirantised between vowels across morpheme boundaries (p > [β], q > [ʁ])
coda obstruents agree in voicing with a following obstruent
high vowels are reduced and often dropped in non-final syllables
/ɑ/ and /ə/ are fronted in non-initial syllables, so that late /ɑ/ can approach [æ]
labial harmony is gradient and optional: after a rounded vowel /ə/ may round to [ʊ] and /ɪ/ to [ʏ]; it is not written
suffix-initial /l n m/ harden to [d t b p] after consonants (-лар, -дар, -тар)
[f v h] occur in Russian and Arabic loans; [h] varies with [χ]
phonotactics: CV is the usual syllable in polysyllables; content monosyllables are CVC
no onset clusters in native words; loan clusters get an intrusive vowel (кран)
coda clusters need a sonorant first member, a voiceless second member and the same place of articulation (бұлт, қарт); other clusters are broken by a vowel (халық)
palatal (backness) harmony within roots and across suffixes; /æ/ is mostly limited to first syllables

stress.type: disputed: traditionally fixed final; others describe initial intensity plus final pitch prominence, or phrase-level prominence only
stress.rule: Traditional descriptions put stress on the last syllable of the word, with some unstressable suffixes and particles; the production study of McCollum & Chen (2021) found no final pitch rise and only marginal evidence for initial prominence.
stress.cues: vowel duration increases from the first to the last syllable (possibly final lengthening); intensity and F0 are highest on the initial syllable

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: the short high vowels /ə ɪ ʊ ʏ/ are reduced and often dropped in non-final syllables; full vowels keep their quality
rhythm.notes: McCollum & Chen (2021) give mean durations of 78 ms (initial), 92 ms (medial) and 132 ms (final syllable) for /ɑ/, and 33, 42 and 77 ms for /ə/.

length.notes: No long versus short pairs of the same quality, but the full vowels are about twice as long as the high vowels (McCollum & Chen 2021). Geminates arise at morpheme boundaries.

voice_onset_time_ms.source: McCollum & Chen 2021, Table 1 (one female speaker, n = 73)

intonation.declarative: gradual decline of F0 through the utterance
intonation.yes_no_question: rise of F0 at the end of the phrase, on the question enclitic (ма/ме, ба/бе, па/пе)
intonation.wh_question: rising F0 on the question word
intonation.continuation: rise at the end of non-final phrases
intonation.accent_shape: no clear word-level pitch accent; F0 falls through the word in the data of McCollum & Chen (2021)

problems: у is always the glide [w], also after a consonant, so су 'water' comes out as [sw] with no vowel (expected [suw])

ы is the schwa phoneme @, which eSpeak cannot stress: words ending in a ы-syllable are stressed earlier (жұлдыз gets initial stress) and words whose only vowels are ы or и get no stress at all (қыз, ит)
и is always [əj], also in front-vowel words (киім)
ө has the short duration of the high vowels (100 against 200) although it is a full mid vowel; the short set should be ы і ұ ү
every л that does not stand directly before a front vowel is dark [ɫ], so codas of front-vowel words are velarised (ел, көл)
ь and ъ are read as glottal stops
t is the unaspirated base2 stop while p and k use aspirated samples
no spirantisation of plosives between vowels and no labial harmony (both gradient in the language)
good: the vowels æ ɵ ʉ ʊ ə ɪ are all present, with short durations for the high vowels
қ, ғ, ң are [q], [ʁ], [ŋ]; е is diphthongal
final stress with a last-syllable rule

notes: The voice is marked 'status testing' in eSpeak NG. Formant and VOT values come from a single female speaker and should not be used as male targets. [f v h] are loan consonants.
